content: I notice that in Mathlib.Algebra.Group.End, right below docs#MulAut.congr, there's some duplicated MulAut and AddAut lemmas. They can't be generated by to_additive as is, since we put a multiplicative structure on both groups. Is there some incantation to fix this?
Oh found it, to_additive_dont_translate
#36156
I need help, I have no idea how to fix the build errors

There's a remark right above docs#Set.conj_mem_fixingSubgroup:

/-
FIXME: The use of `to_additive` in this section is a horrible mess.
It requires translating `MulAut.instGroup` to `AddAut.instAddGroup` instead of `AddAut.instGroup`,
and `MulAut.conj` shouldn't be able to translate to `AddAut.conj`, but somehow it works out.
-/
Maybe the fix here is to translate multiplication on MulAut to addition on AddAut? This would go against mathematical convention I know, but it would make things much easier.
The main issue seems to be docs#MulAut.conj, which we aren't able to translate as docs#AddAut.conj in the current design.

One big issue that I've run into is that we want MulAct G to act on G, and we would like to_additive to translate this into an action of AddAut G on G when G is additive (e.g., these actions for good proofs of lemmas about normal subgroups and normalizers). So whatever translated structure you put on AddAut should also come with a translated action.
But I don't think we have any good additive version of docs#MulDistribMulAction?
i suppose the specific issue with MulAut.conj is that we want MonoidHom to translate to AddChar when the right argument doesn't translate?

Would anything break if we just made the structure on AddAut additive? And if we left some sort of comment "for technical reasons, we break mathematical convention and implement an additive structure instead of a multiplicative one"
Not off the top of my head, although would we need to make a typeclass AddDistribAddAction?

I wrote the quoted comment in a PR not too long ago. My assessment was indeed that MulAut.conj cannot be translated to AddAut.conj. But there are a couple of declarations where this translation IS unexpectedly somehow succeeding. So my suggestion would be to un-to_additivize these declarations. But I couldn't figure out how to do this, because the proof used the group tactic which has no additive counterpart.

maybe we should do this
This to_additive problem is currently blocking quite a lot of work. If anyone has a better fix, they're welcome to suggest it. Otherwise I'll make a PR to additivize AddAut.

IIUC we want MulAut G to be translated to Additive (AddAut G), and for the Additive part to be canceled where possible.
E.g. def MulAut.conj : G →* MulAut G becomes def AddAut.conj : G →+ Additive (AddAut G),
but instance : Group (MulAut G) becomes instance : AddGroup (Additive (AddAut G)) and then AddGroup+Additive cancel each other to get instance : Group (AddAut G).

Is it possible to add such a feature to to_additive, where we define such cancellative pairs? (another example is Additive G₁ →+ Additive G₂ should cancel to give G₁ →* G₂)
No this is not currently in scope for to_additive.

we want MulAut G to be translated to Additive (AddAut G)

the easiest way to accomplish this is by just making the structure on AddAut G additive :upside_down:
Then it sounds like the best solution, and if and when to_additive supports such a fancy feature we'll "fix" AddAut

Violeta Hernández said:

This to_additive problem is currently blocking quite a lot of work. If anyone has a better fix, they're welcome to suggest it. Otherwise I'll make a PR to additivize AddAut.

What work is this blocking? Can we decide to live with the code duplication of MulAut/AddAut?
That is blocked on the fact that there is no add_group tactic.

Floris van Doorn said:

What work is this blocking? Can we decide to live with the code duplication of MulAut/AddAut?

This will mean that every theorem that uses them must be duplicated because to_additive doesn't work. This grows quite quickly, automorphisms are useful
No, this only affects declarations where translation involves adding Additive, which isn't than many.
docs#MulAut.conj is used quite a lot, actually.
That is enough to cause a lot of downstream problems
(deleted)
But is it used in a lot of declarations that are tagged with to_additive?
It is used in declarations that we would like to tag to_additive, but can't currently be

I wanted to additivize docs#ProfiniteGrp.profiniteCompletion in order to define Z^\widehat{\mathbb Z}Z, but somewhere in the long list of declarations missing additive versions MulAut.conj was involved, so breakage ensued
For another example, see _root_.AddSubgroup.mem_normalizer_iff_conj_image_eq and _root_.AddSubgroup.normalizer_le_normalizer_closure in #36760 which I've had to manually translate because of this.

Although interestingly, normal_subgroupOf_closure_normalizer uses normalizer_le_normalizer_closure but to_additive works on it. Somehow to_additive picks up on the translated versions, even though they aren't tagged with to_additive existing and have the wrong type.

Thanks a lot! Sorry I didn't get to this earlier, I got distracted by other Lean projects.

I'm sorry to see that docs#AddAut is made an additive group in #39884. I think all operations from composition should be multiplicative rather than additive. After all docs#Function.End and docs#AddMonoid.End are multiplicative monoids and not additive ones. Changing docs#AddAut to additive creates discrepancy between AddMonoid.End and AddAut, making it impossible to additivize MulAut G ≃* (Monoid.End G)ˣ (which I'm currently adding) to AddAut G ≃* (AddMonoid.End G)ˣ.

What do you think about reverting #39884? Notice that theorems about AddMonoid.End are generated by to_additive, so it should still be possible to use to_additve when AddAut is given a multiplicative operation.

Reverting it will lead to lots of duplication and pain manually additivizing theorems, which is also not good.

How about

or is that too far

Edit: nope, End is not just group but also a ring, so we can't additivize

Junyan Xu said:

What do you think about reverting #39884? Notice that theorems about AddMonoid.End are generated by to_additive, so it should still be possible to use to_additve when AddAut is given a multiplicative operation.

If you can multiplicativize docs#AddAut without breaking things like docs#AddSubgroup.mem_normalizer_iff_map_addConj_eq, then by all means. But the reason for #39884 was that we couldn't find any other alternative that allowed for automatic to_additivization of conjugation arguments in group theory.

Is the main difficulty from MulAut/AddAut.conj? (Sorry if I missed something from previous discussions which I only skimmed.) We might add a plain function version, or since Additive/Multiplicative are type synonyms, it looks to me that it should just translate? Maybe it's best for me to just try and report back ...

Yes, basically there are plenty of times in group theory where you want to consider conjugation automorphisms (e.g., in proving Subgroup.normalizer_le_normalizer_closure), and we don't want to have to rewrite the additive proof every time. So if you can find an alternate way, do let us know!

I think I'm going to change def conj [AddGroup G] : G →+ Additive (AddAut G) to def conj [AddGroup G] : Multiplicative G →* AddAut G (it has been changed to def addConj [AddGroup G] : G →+ AddAut G via to_additive in #39884)

and should we just translate MulDistribMulAction to DistribMulAction ... (indeed it was so before #39884)
Good luck, but I suspect any extra Multiplicative or Additive will break tactic-mode proofs.
Does to_additive use tactic-mode proofs and not just the terms they produce? It has been working before the add_group tactic existed?
Hmm, perhaps you're right. I just feel I've run into trouble with this exact issue before.

We might add a plain function version

I think I'll go with this instead, and rename the bundled versions to Mul/AddAut.conjHom, since even though to_additive can presumably translate the proofs, it can't insert Multiplicative.to/ofAdd to make the additivized statements type correct (up to reducible defeq).

Junyan Xu said:

making it impossible to additivize MulAut G ≃* (Monoid.End G)ˣ

It also seems impossible to additivize A ≃* (Monoid.End B)ˣ, so this seems unrelated to MulAut/AddAut.

The issue is that AddMonoid.End should be the additive version of Monoid.End, but it isn't, and AddMonoid.End is also a Ring so we can't additivize without losing the Ring structure.

(I think the additive part is pointwise operations? 1 is fun x ↦ x, 0 is fun _ ↦ 0, multiplication is composition, addition is pointwise addition fun x ↦ f₁ x + f₂ x)

Do we know if Ring (AddMonoid.End M) is used a lot?

I think Ring (AddMonoid.End M) is fine, and we're even adding the categorical version at #43539.

Indeed it seems it's impossible to connect A ≃* (Monoid.End B)ˣ and Multiplicative A ≃* (AddMonoid.End B)ˣ via to_additive. I tried to connect G →* MulAut G and Multiplicative G →* AddAut G or G →+ Additive (AddAut G) and both failed, even though this should work up to defeq ...

The Ring instance is the blocker here, wdym by "fine"?
If it's not so commonly used, perhaps we could move it to a type-alias?

The endomorphism ring is definitely important. And it shows we don't want addition to be composition; instead we want it to come from the codomain.

My refactor attempt is now at #44244, awaiting CI.
MulAut G ≃* (Monoid.End G)ˣ has been added and additivized successfully in the latest commit.
CI is green now with +147 / -153 diff.
What's the refactor here? Are we ensuring that anything that goes through conj remains additivizable?
The refactor is that conj is now a plain function instead of a group homomorphism

conj is turned into a plain function so it's trivially additivizable. conj_one/mul/inv simp lemmas are added to replace map_one/mul/inv. The original MulAut.conj/AddAut.addConj is turned into conjHom/addConjHom, but they can no longer be connected by to_additive even though there seems to be no defeq obstruction.

By the way, we currently have the cursed situation that MulDistribMulAction is tagged to_additive to translate to AddDistribAddAction in the file where it is defined, but later it gets another to_additive attribute to translate to DistribMulAction instead.

Do you know whether we need to keep both attributes around? For now, to_additive/to_dual are not meant to support having multiple translations for a single constant.

I've moved DistribMulAction to the same file as MulDistribMulAction and removed the translation to AddDistribAddAction. It would be reasonable to translate DistribSMul to MulDistribSMul, but the latter is yet to be defined; if everyone agrees I can do in the same PR.

conjHom/addConjHom, but they can no longer be connected by to_additive even though there seems to be no defeq obstruction.

More explicitly the following fails

@[simps] def _root_.AddAut.addConjHom [AddGroup G] : G →+ Additive (AddAut G) where
  toFun := .ofMul ∘ AddAut.addConj
  map_add' _ _ := by ext; simp [AddAut.addConj, add_assoc]
  map_zero' := by ext; simp [AddAut.addConj]

@[to_additive existing, simps] def conjHom [Group G] : G →* MulAut G where
  toFun := conj
  map_mul' _ _ := by ext; simp [conj, mul_assoc]
  map_one' := by ext; simp [conj]

with the error message

`to_additive` validation failed: expected
  {G : Type ?u.1} → [inst : AddGroup G] → G →+ AddAut G
but 'AddAut.addConjHom' has type
  {G : Type u_3} → [inst : AddGroup G] → G →+ Additive (AddAut G)

But the two things are defeq (non-reducibly of course). Is the error because to_additive work only up to reducible defeq?

It is true that to_additive checks for reducible defeq here. But even if this to_additive existing could be made to work, then using to_additive with this translation conjHom -> addConjHom will give weird expressions, if it even works at all.
@Junyan Xu, I've opened #44266 (feat(Translate): improve translation heuristic) which should fix the issue you encountered with to_additive.
(replying to your previous message, somehow failed to send) It can be used in proofs but not statements (that's why I need plain function in statements to keep to_additive working).
#44244 now compiles after merging master. Two lemmas mentioning the conjugation homomorphism can no longer be to_additivized. And another possibly unexpected behavior of to_additive is found.

It's still a bit unfortunate that this would result in being unable to automatically additivize proofs that mention the conjugation homomorphism. Is keeping the additive AddAut around for this purpose a viable option? (e.g., don't write any API for it besides what's generated automatically by @[to_additive])
